facts.statement: Gallina and Apesteguía described Cathartesaura in 2005 based on a partial skeleton containing vertebrae and limb bones.
facts.quote: The fossil remains, described by Gallina and Apesteguía in 2005, consist of a partial skeleton including vertebrae and limb bones.

facts.statement: Cathartesaura lived during the Early Cretaceous in the Huincul Formation of the Neuquén Basin in Río Negro Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: Cathartesaura is a genus of rebbachisaurid sauropod dinosaur from Early Cretaceous strata of the Huincul Formation, at the "La Buitrera" locality, in the Neuquén Basin of Río Negro Province, Argentina.

facts.statement: Fossils of Cathartesaura were found in mudstone and sandstone layers dating to the Albian stage at the base of the formation.
facts.quote: These were found at the base of the formation, which dates back to the Albian stage, in mudstone and sandstone levels.

facts.statement: The genus name Cathartesaura combines the New World vulture genus Cathartes with the Greek word for lizard.
facts.quote: The generic name is composed of Cathartes, the New World vulture genus and -saura, feminine declination of the Greek term sauros, "lizard".

facts.statement: The species name anaerobica honors the Argentinian adhesive company Anaeróbicos for supporting the fossil extraction and preparation.
facts.quote: The specific epithet honors the Argentinian adhesive company Anaeróbicos for providing field and laboratory support during the extraction and preparation of the fossils.

facts.statement: Cathartesaura was a medium-sized herbivore with a long, lightly built, well-muscled neck that had limited vertical movement.
facts.quote: Cathartesaura is a medium-sized herbivorous dinosaur with a long, lightly built, well-muscled neck albeit with a somewhat limited range of dorso-ventral movement.

facts.statement: Cathartesaura is distinguished by vertebral features like bony laminae associations and pneumatic chambers in the neck that link it to Rebbachisauridae.
facts.quote: C. anaerobica has distinguishing characteristics in the vertebrae that ally it with Rebbachisauridae, such as the bony laminae association and the pneumatic chambers in the cervical series.

facts.statement: Its discovery alongside other rebbachisaurids, the only diplodocoid group in the early Late Cretaceous, supports the idea that an extinction event eliminated diplodocoids, allowing saltasaurine titanosaurs to fill their niche.
facts.quote: Being found in early Late Cretaceous sediments, along with other rebbachisaurids, the only diplodocoid group of the time, this find helps cement the notion that a subsequent extinction event wiped out these remaining diplodocoid dinosaurs leaving saltasaurine titanosaurs to occupy the vacant ecological niche.

facts.statement: Cathartesaura belongs to the subfamily Limaysaurinae.
Cathartesaura is classified in the family Rebbachisauridae.
Cathartesaura is a member of the class Saurischia.
Cathartesaura lived between 110.1 and 106.3 million years ago during the Albian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (110.1 to 106.3 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The name references the turkey vulture, Cathartes aura, whose Spanish name 'buitre' was used to name the fossil locality because of the abundance of these birds there.
rejected.quote: It also implies the juxtaposition of the components of the scientific name of the turkey vulture, Cathartes aura, whose Spanish name, "buitre", named the locality where the fossil was found due to the abundance of such birds there.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'the turkey vulture Cathartes aura whose Spanish name'
